title: A neighboring vista of stellar birth
caption: Part of the N159 star-forming complex, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: LMC N159 · constellation Dorado · about 160000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A thick column of black dust runs through the center, blocking stars that light it from behind. Paler clouds glow beyond, layered red filaments spread to either side, and blue, white and gold stars shine through it all. This is part of N159, a star-forming complex in the Large Magellanic Cloud, about 160000 light-years away.

Hubble captured this field in parallel with a recently released image, so it shows a neighboring patch of the same complex. Cold hydrogen gas forms ridges, cavities and glowing filaments. Inside the dense clouds, young stars switch on, and their radiation makes the hydrogen around them glow deep red.
The brightest areas mark hot, massive young stars. Their winds and light hollow out bubbles in the gas, a process astronomers call stellar feedback, as new stars reshape the cloud they formed from.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.44 x 2.34 arcminutes) and distance (160000 light years), the frame spans roughly 114 × 109 light-years. Its light set out about 160,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took V (555 nm) and I (814 nm) images, and Wide Field Camera 3 added a hydrogen-alpha image at 656 nm. The packet does not publish how colors were assigned to the filters.
understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter isolates the red glow of hydrogen gas, and long exposures collect far more of this faint light than the eye could.

explore: Among the star-forming clouds of the Large Magellanic Cloud, N159 is one of the most massive. The LMC is a dwarf galaxy and the largest of the small galaxies orbiting the Milky Way. The whole complex stretches over 150 light-years, and this image covers only a portion.
alt: A dark column of dust against glowing clouds, with red filaments on both sides and blue, white and gold stars throughout.
